# OpenMates feature overview

One row per feature, sub-features indented below their parent. Edit `specifications/features.yml`
(grouping, intent, release, notes); everything else is derived from the repository.

Cells with tests are derived: Specification assertion → tests on that surface → latest CI result
(`specifications/test-results.yml`, results as of 2026-11-16).
**live** = all counted assertions pass and the feature is on in production · tested = all pass ·
partial = some pass · **FAIL** = a test failed in its latest run · not run = tests exist, no CI result.
x/y = passing / counted assertions (required on that surface by the Specification, or tested there).
Cells without tests show the human intent: impl = implemented, untested · wip · planned · ? = unverified · — = not planned.
Flags: dev/prod enablement from committed config (`backend_config.dev.yml` / `backend_config.yml`).
Apple covers the shared iOS, iPadOS and macOS app (TestFlight); Watch is shown where relevant.
Parity gaps per surface: `python3 scripts/feature_overview.py gaps --surface apple`.

### Chat Drafts

### Chat-bound Voice And Video Calls
<a id="video-call"></a>

Voice and video calls with the assistant, bound to an encrypted chat.

- Specifications: [feature.video-call](../../specifications/features/video-call/specification.yml) (draft), [feature.video-call-experiment](../../specifications/features/video-call-experiment/specification.yml) (superseded) · 59 assertion(s)
- Flags: none · dev on (no flag) · prod on (no flag) · release v0.19.0
- Notes: Clients that opt in at call start (likely_end_hints) receive turn.likely_end / turn.resumed hints from the server; the web app with the Rust core opts in and lets the core prepare the turn early, dropping that preparation on turn.resumed. Apple does not opt in yet. The voice-call web spec is the key end-to-end test. Spoken tap requests (needs-you chime, ready-made line, 15 s reminder, 30 s memory self-cancel with a timed-out event; video-call.chat.permission-prompt) are web-only so far; the Apple app ignores the voice_call_permission_prompt event.
